edges.effect_quant: The pancreatic-cancer evidence is thinner than the colorectal signal, but available syntheses generally place higher whole-grain intake on the lower-risk side.
edges.mechanism: Whole grains improve carbohydrate quality and fiber exposure in ways that may reduce chronic hyperinsulinemia and associated pancreatic stress. That mechanism is plausible, but the epidemiologic base is still too limited for high-confidence claims.
edges.summary: The direct observational meta-analysis reported lower pancreatic-cancer risk with higher whole-grain intake. Broader whole-grain umbrella reviews did not contradict that direction, so the most careful reading is an encouraging but still lower-confidence protective association.
edges.caveats: The underlying evidence base is much smaller than for whole grains and colorectal cancer, and residual dietary-pattern confounding is substantial. This edge should be interpreted as supportive rather than definitive.
